**Note on comparability:** 3M completed the spin-off of its Health Care business (Solventum) on April 1, 2024. As a result, the FY2024 10-K restates FY2023 revenue to exclude Solventum (reported as discontinued operations), producing a comparable FY2023 figure of $24,610 million — very different from the $32,681 million originally reported in the FY2023 10-K [DOC: mmm_fy2023_10k.txt]. Because of this divestiture/spin-off, the two "FY2023" figures are not on the same accounting basis, and only the restated (continuing-operations) comparison in the FY2024 filing is apples-to-apples with FY2024 results.

- FY2024 total revenue: $24,575 million [DOC: mmm_fy2024_income_statement.txt]
- FY2023 total revenue, restated for comparability (excluding Solventum/Health Care, reported as discontinued operations): $24,610 million [DOC: mmm_fy2024_income_statement.txt]
- FY2023 total revenue as originally reported (including Health Care/Solventum, before spin-off): $32,681 million [DOC: mmm_fy2023_10k.txt]

Using the comparable, restated continuing-operations basis (the correct like-for-like comparison given the Solventum spin-off) [DOC: mmm_fy2024_notes.txt]:

Revenue growth = ($24,575M − $24,610M) / $24,610M ≈ −0.14% (a slight decline, not growth)

If instead one naively compares FY2024 to the originally reported FY2023 figure (which is NOT a valid comparison because it includes the now-divested Health Care/Solventum business), revenue would appear to fall by about 24.8% — but this comparison is misleading and not recommended due to the change in reporting basis from the spin-off.

ANSWER: On a comparable (continuing-operations) basis, 3M's revenue was essentially flat to slightly down, declining about 0.14% from $24,610M in FY2023 (restated) to $24,575M in FY2024 — i.e., no real growth. (Note: this is not comparable to the originally reported FY2023 figure of $32,681M, which included the Health Care/Solventum business that was spun off in April 2024.)
